styleGuide.visualStyle: Clean flat 2D vector on a deep navy space background with a few small static stars. A simple flat Earth seen from orbit (blue ocean, muted green landmasses, no texture). Satellites are friendly minimal icons; signals are pulsing concentric rings travelling outward. Trilateration is shown on a flat, simplified map with expanding circles in teal, coral and gold. Clocks are simple dials or digital readouts. The user's location is always a bright blue dot (#3D8BFF) with a soft halo. Short labels only, generous spacing, smooth ease-in-out motion.
styleGuide.fontFamily: Inter (semibold for labels, bold for titles), fallback: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
styleGuide.iconStyle: Flat minimal icons with rounded corners and 3px rounded strokes, no gradients or shadows. Satellites are a small rounded body with two rectangular solar panels; the phone is a rounded rectangle with a map screen. Use palette colours only, plus the location blue #3D8BFF for the user's dot.

scenes.layout: Opens full-frame on a phone screen in the centre showing a simplified map with the blue dot. The camera then pulls back: the phone shrinks to the lower centre on a small Earth, and a satellite icon appears high in the upper right, linked to the phone by a dashed distance line with a label beside it.
scenes.visualDescription: A familiar blue location dot pulses on a phone map, with a small accuracy ring around it. Zooming out reveals the Earth below and a satellite far overhead, with a dashed line showing how far away it is.

scenes.layout: Satellite in the upper left, Earth arc at the bottom with the phone standing on it at lower right. Signal rings travel diagonally down from satellite to phone. Two small tags travel in a straight line along the invisible satellite-to-phone path, just ahead of the leading ring.
scenes.visualDescription: A satellite sends out pulsing rings toward the phone. Two little tags, a position pin and a clock, glide straight down the satellite-to-phone path just in front of the leading ring, staying upright and readable. As they reach the phone, a small sound-wave receive badge on the phone lights up with the label 'Only listens'. A crossed-out upward arrow shows the phone sends nothing back.

scenes.visualDescription: Two digital clocks compare the departure and arrival times of one signal pulse. The tiny gap between them is highlighted, then the simple equation 'distance = time x speed of light' assembles and the travel path turns into a measured distance.

scenes.layout: Flat top-down simplified map filling the frame, with three small satellite markers (teal A, coral B, gold C) at different spots around the edges; circles expand from each. The final point is near the centre. A small rounded label chip sits in the upper left. For the 3D beat, the map tilts in flat 2D: it scales vertically to about 55% with a slight horizontal skew, so the map circles become flat ellipses lying on it.
scenes.visualDescription: Trilateration on a map: a teal circle shows every spot at the first distance. A coral circle crosses it at two points. A gold circle passes through only one of them, and the blue dot appears there. Then the map tilts back (squashed vertically, slightly skewed) and each circle becomes a flat ellipse on the map, the 'equator' of a sphere. Around each equator a full upright circle outline with about 20% opacity fill appears, so each one reads as a sphere. All three still overlap at the blue dot. Everything stays flat: solid fills with opacity, no gradients or shading.

Small rounded surface-colour chip in the upper left whose text reads '2D: circles' and then changes to '3D: spheres'.

scenes.layout: Title question at top centre. Centre-right: the same tilted map from the end of s05 (about 55% vertical scale, slight skew) with the same three satellite markers A, B and C and their rings drawn as flat ellipses. Lower left: a small rounded surface-colour inset card holding the phone and its cheap clock dial. A fourth satellite marker enters the tilted map from the right edge.
scenes.visualDescription: We stay in the tilted map view from s05, showing just the three flat ellipse rings so it is easy to read; the blue dot is replaced by a faint dashed outline marking the true spot. In the inset, the phone's cheap clock slips by a tiny coral tick. All three rings grow by the same amount and still meet at one point, but it is a hollow 'ghost' dot that has slid about 300 m away from the true spot. The rings pulse together because they share the same error. A white fourth satellite slides in, and its ring clearly misses the ghost dot, leaving a small coral gap. The clock hand nudges back, all four rings shrink together and meet at a single point on the true spot, where the blue dot pops in with 'Clock fixed'.

elements.description: Title 'Why 4 satellites?' at top centre.

Small rounded surface-colour card, lower left: phone icon beside a simple analogue clock dial. A small coral 'tick' offset wedge beside the hand shows it slightly off, with a tiny '1 µs off' label under the dial.

The tilted s05 map with satellite markers A (teal), B (coral) and C (gold), each with its distance ring drawn as a flat ellipse in its colour (3px stroke, no fill). A faint dashed white outline circle marks the true spot where the blue dot was in s05.
Hollow coral-outlined dot where the three grown rings meet, with a thin dashed coral line back to the true spot and the label '~300 m off'.

Fourth satellite marker in text colour (white) with its own white flat ellipse ring on the tilted map. When it first appears its ring passes just beside the ghost dot, and a short coral bracket highlights the gap.
Blue location dot (#3D8BFF) on the true spot, with a 'Clock fixed' label beside it.

scenes.layout: Phone map in the centre with the blue dot moving along a street. For the recap, three short labels line up in a row across the bottom third, connected by arrows.
scenes.visualDescription: Back on the phone map, the blue dot glides smoothly along a street as tiny signal rings keep arriving. Then a three-step recap appears beneath: satellites send time, time becomes distance, four distances find you, ending on the pulsing blue dot.
